   PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!
Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!
The easiest for us to edit are
Tasword 2 files with the right
margin set at 32 but a textfile
in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use
our discretion anyway. Letters
may also be edited for clarity
and length... Please ask if you
welcome direct correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

From H. Matthews, KINGTON





Dear Ron,


Firstly, may I say how much I've
enjoyed OUTLET since my first
introduction in October, 1991. I
have found much to amuse and
inform me  -  I have found the
Masterfile Plus 3 particularly
useful but I have a query...


How can I put a listing which is
in the form of an array such as
"names" DATA a$() in Masterfile?


I have recently purchased second
hand a keyboard with Midi and I
have managed to change the Music
BASIC-type listings to the form
"Y1Ncdga"etc but I am completely
defeated by machine code list-
ings. Is there any way to enable
such machine code music to be
played through the Midi connect-
ion?

I hope you can help or "know who
can"!

        Yours sincerely,

          H. Matthew

Brian Cavers to H. Matthew




If the data file is a 48K MAST-
ERFILE file then you should be
able to convert it to an ASCII
file using the CONV file that
comes with the MASTERFILE +3
program in OUTLET 76. It can
then be loaded into MF3 using
the IMPORT feature. CONV might
be tried on other data files but
I have not used it I must admit
and you may well have to do a
bit of experimenting.

If the data is not lengthy you
may be better off printing it
and typing it in again!


Machine code programs control
the sound chip directly and use
their own routines for MIDI. It
would need a lot of experience
to change such programs.The port
addresses to control the sound
chip and the MID interface are
given near the bottom of page
180 of the +3 manual. However,
there are no details of how they
are controlled. It may be a bit
is set when sending a byte to a
register. Even if we had this
technical information it would
still need some skill to modify
any existing programs.

Has anyone else any information
on this?
                      Brian

From Mark Battison, LONDON SE25


Dear Chezron,

Slowly but surely, I am catching
up with last year's OUTLETS and
I'm very impresed with each one.
There are some things which I
find too technical  - or not of
interest (yet!)  but there are
still many things in each issue
which are interesting, useful or
both.

1994 was the year of the comput-
er (and disk drive) breakdowns
Which means that I have had a
full system up and running for
only about two months  - on and
off  - since last May!!


The computer I am using at the
moment is a Spanish +2A.It works
perfectly OK (with headphones as
there is no built-in speaker)
apart from the messages and re-
ports being in Spanish.It is not
difficult to interpret things
like "2 VARIABLE NO DEFINA" or
"9 SENTENCIA STOP". +D messages
are in English.


I must apologize for the lack of
contributions (letters or art-
icles) lately. Assuming no more
breakdowns (praying...) I should
be able to get in touch shortly.

Anyway, I'm glad to see there is
no lack of conributions from
other readers.


Keep up the good work and best
wishes for 1995.

         Best Regards,

         Mark Battison


P.S.This was written on THE LAST
WORD- the new wordprocessor from
Myrmidon Software.This is a very
good wordprocessor which works
with minimal modification on the
Plus D.

Brian Cavers to Mark Battison

When you enter RANDOMIZE USR 0
on your Spanish computer does it
give the error message...
"Hasta La Vista, Baby!". Just a
thought.

Regarding contributions, why not
send in a review - or at least a
summary (or even the name and
address of Myrmidon and price!)-
of THE LAST WORD?  Is that the
same THE LAST WORD issued by the
keyboard firm SAGA years ago and
republished in 1989 by Trojan
Software? If so, I wonder if it
is the VERY last word.  Where
did you hear about it? There are
not many places left to advert-
ise.
                          Brian

From David S. Williams, CARDIFF



Dear Sir,

I hope you can spare the time to
help me with a problem I have in
attempting to connect a Spectrum
+3 via the RGB/Peritel socket,to
either a Sanyo Model DM8112CX,
Taxan KX-117,or a similar'green'
VDU monitor which will run  with
computers that  have  composite
video outputs.

I have been advised to make the
following connections from the
two wires from the 8-pin plug:
earth to 2, run other to 6 and
short 4, 6, 7, 8 together.


I enclose a  photocopied  sheet
from the +3 manual and this
seems to bear out the idea, but
all I am getting from a  lead
made to these specifications is
a bright green screen on  the
Sanyo and Taxan.

I have consulted quite a few
people including Format magazine
and it appears that the wiring
should work.  However,  perhaps
somone out there  makes leads
that are known to work - I would
willingly purchase one to  save
further hassle with this prob-
lem.

        Yours sincerely,

       David S. Williams

Brian Cavers to David Williams


I recommend you ring the follow-
ing suppliers and ask for their
advice. In particular, the first
one listed was recommended by a
reader so try them first. I urge
you to note down any details of
your system and monitors you can
so you are ready to answer any
questions. For example, check
the back of your monitors and
note down the type of connectors
etc...

From Francis G. Miles, WELWYN




Dear Ron and Brian,


Reading through OUTLET back num-
bers I came across the following
query, which I don't think ever
got answered:


When you load one program from
within another (like CATLOADER),
if the loaded program doesn't
autorun you get a "Nonsense in
BASIC" message. Is there any way
round this? (Paul Oliver, OUT-
LETTER in OUTLET 39)


Well, you can SAVE...LINE 10000,
ie autorunning at the nonexist-
ent line 10000. This LOADs just
like a non-autorunning program,
and if you LOAD it from CATLOAD-
ER you get an "OK" message.There
might be other complications,but
I can't think of any.

As a matter of interest, SAVE...
LINE x has this effect with any
value of x from 10000 to 13683.
You might prefer 11111, it's
easier to type. If x is from
13684 (ie 4000 hex) to 65535, it
produces a normal non-autorun-
ning program,  just as if you'd
not used any LINE function at
all - and it also makes a Nons-
ense report from CATLOADER. SAVE
... LINE 0 operates as if you'd
done SAVE ... LINE 1.

  OUTLETTER - BACK TO THE PAST

Good question:  What could you
carry back in your time machine
worth `100,000 in today's money
which would be worth `100,000 in
money of the past?

It reminds me of SMUGGLING,
about which I once did a little
research - not that I wanted to
join in, but it was interfering
with my customers' business.

Smugglers,to make their business
worthwhile, need a product which

(a) is cheap to buy in the coun-
try of origin and very expensive
in the destination country, and


(b) is very compact, so that
`10,000, or preferably `100,000
worth, will fit in the bottom of
a rowing boat and can be dumped
in the sea with minimum effort
if the Customs and Excise loom
up.

The smugglers I was interested
in were operating between Muscat
& Oman and Karachi (Pakistan) or
Bombay (India) but I daresay the
same rules apply anywhere.

They were carrying Japanese-made
glitter thread (Lurex type -
it's made of plastic film, would
you believe); there was a terri-
fic demand in India and Pakistan
for wedding saris, but both Gov-
ernments had put on ferocious
import restrictions.

These smugglers didn't carry
heroin,  which was cheaper if
anything in India than it was in
Oman;  but you can see how on
some routes it's an attractive
commodity. They carried gold
sometimes, when the market was
right.

Seems to me that Brian with his
time machine is setting up as a
TIME SMUGGLER  (good SF title
there). What should he carry? He
rules out any twentieth-century
technology,no doubt to avoid any
"time warps"which might kill off
his grandfather, etc. I suppose
I must agree with him; I'd love
to take a Spectrum to show
Charles Babbage and Lady Love-
lace - but how could you plug it
in?

Unmounted jewels:uncut diamonds?
Of dubious value in time travel,
because `100,000 worth in 1990
might only fetch `1,000 in the
un-devalued money of 1690. The
same applies to silver and gold,
whether in antique or modern
forms.

Platinum or similar exotic met-
als? Well, yes:aluminium fetched
`16 an ounce in 1864, when Jules
Verne published his story about
Americans going to the moon in
an aluminium capsule. You'd have
a hell of a marketing problem,
though: who wanted to buy alumi-
nium, apart from the fictional
Gun Club of Baltimore, and what
could they do with it, in 1864,
let alone in 1690?


Purple dye? W H Perkin invented
synthetic aniline dyes (by mis-
take) in 1856. Up to then nearly
all dyes were of vegetable ori-
gin  (oh,  all right,  "Tyrian
purple"  was made of shellfish).
For example,  denim cloth for
blue jeans was dyed with indigo,
a quite expensive herb mostly
grown in the Third World (it was
big in South Carolina from the
1740s till Perkin killed the
trade).

But synthetic indigo wasn't the
first aniline dye:  this was
"mauve",a name invented for this
hitherto unknown colour by Perk-
in (or by his marketing depart-
ment).  Till then, women had
dressed in clothes coloured with


vegetable dyes:  in 1860 or so
they were suddenly all wearing
mauve.  It must have been horr-
ible.  Thank God no one thought
of using it for jeans.

Still,  a professional smuggler
wouldn't look at aniline dyes
for time smuggling:  too bulky,
and again too hard to market.

No, you'd need to do some care-
ful historical market research -
not too different from what act-
ual smugglers do.

The results might be surprising.
For example, if you were going
to any time before about 1650,
your best freight might well be
black peppercorns...


Half a hundredweight of black
peppercorns wouldn't take up too
much room, would sell like hot
cakes (literally, I suppose) and
would set you up for life.  Pep-
per was hideously expensive, and
much in demand for masking the
flavour of the salt meat and
fish people used to eat in win-
ter.

But this wouldn't be worthwhile
after the Indies trade had prop-
erly begun to get going.

Or of course if you could get to
Holland, some fancy tulip bulbs.

        Yours sincerely,

        FRANCIS G MILES

Brian Cavers to Francis Miles

One of the nice features of the
SAM Coupe's BASIC is an option
to LOAD... LINE equivalent to
the SAVE... LINE. I used it very
often with a high line number to
prevent an autoload program from
running but it could be used to
stop a non-autload program from
giving an error.

Incidentally, the highest line
number on the SAM is 655279
(which is one less than 255 x
256 = 655280 thus leaving the
255 high byte to mark the end of
BASIC if I remember correctly).
Oddly though, one could enter up
to 65535 with LOAD... LINE so
you could guarantee being higher
than the highest line.

Yes,  I should have thought of
spices.The difficulty of finding
many such commodities that would
be valuable in previous centur-
ies emphasises the immense power
and value of information. If I
had not set the restriction on
myself I might take the secrets
of the steam engine, internal
combustion engine, aircraft,
dynamos, radio, penicillin,fire-
arms, precision clocks - the
list is endless.
                          Brian

From Cliff Tate, REDCAR





Hi hello,

I am Cliff.

I am dropping down a letter as I
would love some info on the lat-
est Spectrum MAG. I would love
to see how much your OUTLET disc
magazine is so I can see what's
happening in the world of Spec-
trums, as I may buy it now and
again as I am a Spectrum User.

The Spectrums I use are a Spect-
rum +2A and a +3.


I am looking for an  animation
program which,  say I drew a
picture,  it would then make it
animate around the screen, melt-
ing etc.  I'd love some animator
programs so I could make some
smarter demo's etc.  I'd love a
copy if you have any animator
programs with which I could exp-
eriment.

Respect.

See ya! Keep Spectrumming!

Cliff Tate


Brian Cavers to Cliff Tate


I suggest that you scour Micro-
mart adverts - and any computer
fairs you can -to try and spot a
secondhand copy of the ANIMATOR
program that came out years ago.

Another possibility is to try to
get a video digitizer. You might
then snapshot a short sequence
from a cartoon and display the
frames rapidly in sequence using
a simple LDIR machine code rout-
ine. We have two or three lined
up for publication in OUTLET
that use this method - starting
next month while this month is a
similar one using PLOT and DRAW
to create the frames.


I should point out that the demo
type of program is really made
by advanced programmers who want
to explore just what the Spect-
rum can do and push it further.
The advanced demos such as you
see in OUTLET are not merely put
together using a simple drawing
that is "morphed" and "melted"
automatically into pleasing pat-
terns. These demos are written
by expert programmers who write
specific routines to achieve
each effect. True,they do borrow
each others' ideas and even the
code but primarily they are just
very good programmers. Much of
what they do is way beyond my
skills even though I have been
programming for about twelve
years!
                    Brian

From Tony Wilson, YORKS

Dear Ron & Brian,

Please send me Issue 22 ON TAPE!
It's about time I had a look at
the early ones to see if I can
usefully translate them onto +3
disk.

I've tried editing the  CONTENTS
lines 20 and 25 for my own use -
mainly for printing out pre-
TABLOID stuff but all the hidden
code lying around messes up a
listing. Any suggestions?

Cheers,

Tony Wilson


Brian Cavers to Tony Wilson

Sorry, there is no easy way! I
spend all day converting the +D
version to +3 but I still have
to use an A4 checklist sheet as
there are so many complications!
Furthermore, the tape version
has various lines removed and I
have NEVER converted the tape
version to +3. Furthermore, I
have loads of utilities all
customised to help me with the
task of conversion.

However, here are a few tips but
don't expect everything to work
perfectly. I have not tried this
and there are variations and I
may overlook something so expect
some hassle!...


Load LEAVER from OUTLET 79 and
press L to extract the routine.
Save it on a spare disk. Study
it and try it until you under-
stand its use. Hereafter, If I
say something like "extract and
save lines..." I mean, merge
LEAVER and use it to delete the
rest of BASIC but the lines you
want to extract.

Load anything from disk and try
entering SPECTRUM to get to 48K
mode. Then enter RANDOMIZE USR
23354 (Key T, Extend, 23354) to
get back to 128K. Practice this.
You will need to get familiar
with this. If you see any lines
with colours in them then switch
to 48K to edit them and back to
128K to use the disk.


When you break into some OUTLET
programs, the listing may not be
visible. Practice entering...

         POKE 23607,60
                ...blindly until
it is second nature. This will
reveal the listing. An alternate
way is to reset and MERGE the
program. However, some programs
may not permit this.

In almost every case you can
save a program to +3 disk using
RUN 9972 (BUT YOU MUST BE IN 128
MODE!)

Load the tape issue until the
title picture appears.Change the
LOAD "" at the end of line 50 to
LOAD "CONTENTS". Save on disk.


Load the CONTENTS from tape.

Jot down line 9902 for reference
(you might use LLIST 9902 then
break in after that line has
printed).

Extract lines 20 to 30.

Load a recent CONTENTS. Merge in
those lines 20 and 30 and adjust
line 9902 ACCORDING TO YOUR BEST
JUDGEMENT! Sorry but there may
be numerous variations. Save it.

You need a tape header reader to
find the size of code files. Try
CASSCAT from OUTLET 37. I assume
you know how to load and save to
disk but you need to change the
names of some thus...
.

Early text files use the keyword
"CODE" as the 10th character and
this needs changing to "#". If
you find the address and length
of the code using CASSCAT as say
A and L then try something like:

10 LOAD "T:"

20 SAVE "A:"

10 LOAD "NAME     CODE" CODE A,L

20 SAVE "NAME     #" CODE A,L


The CODE and the # must ALWAYS
be the 10th character so put in
spaces if needed. You will have
to enter the CODE keyword in 48K
using EXTEND then I.


Individual programs will probab-
ly load and run except where the
program loads extra code. This
may be OK if the code is named
but not if it is simply....
LOAD "" CODE etc. In that case
you will need to search for the
actual filename using your best
judgement!

If you want the individual prog-
rams to link back to CONTENTS,
NEXT and BOOT properly then
study, in 48K, lines 8920 to
8930 in recent programs to see
how they work. You might then
extract such lines and MERGE
them in old programs. HOWEVER,
there are many, many variations
so lots of possibilities for
errors!


On Side B of any recent +3 disk
is a file called "DISK". This
needs copying to Side B of the
disk you are trying to create.It
simply loads the CONTENTS on the
B side.

This CONTENTS file on Side B is
a slightly modified form of the
one on Side A.I suggest that you
take the one from the same issue
you get the Side A from and alt-
er it in the same way except
line 9902.

In both CONTENTS there are lines
at around 91 to 108 that do var-
ious things like loading OUTDEX,
PROCROSS and the line at 99
which prompts you when to switch
to Side B.


You need to alter the value in
line 99: PEEK NIF > VAL "14" to
the last file you have on Side
A.Just for your reference,Item N
on the CONTENTS display is 14.

Oh yes! -  Nearly forgot!  Alter
the value of H at the start of
line 9930 in CONTENTS to the
total number of filenames listed
in the DATA at line 30. I now
have a horrible feeling the DATA
may have a different sequence!
Compare the originals - you may
need to use a recent line 30 and
retype the filenames!

Those are only the basic things
to worry about but you may get
it to work even if not perfectly
so good luck!             Brian

From Geoff Harris, HALESOWEM,

Dear Outletters,

Let me tell you a story; a story
of patience, learning and frust-
ration. I've been using my +3
for some years both for business
and pleasure, so much, in fact,
that it's an important part of
my life. I added a printer and B
drive and waited for the time
when I could spot a monitor at
the right price (I'm either mean
or careful with money).  What I
really fancied was a colour
portable with all the features
including a SCART socket;  I've
used a basic model through a
switched Y splitter for some
time.


At last the retail prices had
fallen enough and I bought just
what I wanted, or so I thought,
from COLOURVISION at `150 and a
SCART lead through my local home
electronics shop. It didn't work
via the SCART socket! I had the
lead checked.  It was fine and I
contacted the service engineers
of the tv retailers.  This is
where I started to learn...




LESSON ONE

Q. When is a SCART socket not a
SCART socket?

A. When it is "partially wired".


Apparently your common or garden
tv with SCART will input compos-
ite video and not do much else.

A visit to the library taught me
about composite video and PAL
encoding;  Part 1 of Peter John-
son's article also helped.  I
looked forward to Part 2 to find
out how to convert my +3's RGB +
composite sync into a composite
video signal.

Again I was disappointed,  BUT
WAIT! There is a light on the
horizon and its name is Malcolm
Perry. He tells us that there is
a composite video signal avail-
able in the +3 at 4 volt TTL all
we need is the buffer amplifier
that was removed from the +2
when the +3 was designed.

Please Mr. Perry,  or anyone at
all, tell me the configuration
of 3 diodes and a transistor you
mentioned so that my prayers are
answered and I sleep soundly at
night.

I am,
        Yours sincerely,

          Geoff Harris


Brian Cavers to Geoff Harris

Hopefully,someone will soon come
through with an answer. Sorry I
am not much help with many of
these hardware problems.

                        Brian


From G.T. Parkyn, TRURO


Dear Sirs,

Is it safe to switch the printer
to a different computer with the
power on? I have not dared to do
this - assuming that it would be
equivalent to pulling out an
interface with power on with
disastrous results!

             Yours sincerely,

               G.T. Parkyn

Brian Cavers to G.T. Parkyn

Yes, it should be safe so long
as the data switch is not faulty
- Ron has done so for years with
no hardware problems. I had a
glitch last year which I am
pretty certain was a fault with
my PC's I/O card. I got into the
habit of switching my printer
off-line before throwing the
data switch but I now think I am
just being paranoid!

You may occasionally get an odd-
ity with a program testing for
the printer and throwing up an
error message. Obviously, make
sure the current computer is not
trying or waiting to use the
printer.
                         Brian.

Sorry, there is no easy way! I spend all day converting the +D version to +3 but I still have to use an A4 checklist sheet as there are so many complications! Furthermore, the tape version has various lines removed and I have NEVER converted the tape version to +3. Furthermore, I have loads of utilities all customised to help me with the task of conversion.

However, here are a few tips but don't expect everything to work perfectly. I have not tried this and there are variations and I may overlook something so expect some hassle!...

Load LEAVER from OUTLET 79 and press L to extract the routine. Save it on a spare disk. Study it and try it until you under- stand its use. Hereafter, If I say something like "extract and save lines..." I mean, merge LEAVER and use it to delete the rest of BASIC but the lines you want to extract.

Load anything from disk and try entering SPECTRUM to get to 48K mode. Then enter RANDOMIZE USR 23354 (Key T, Extend, 23354) to get back to 128K. Practice this. You will need to get familiar with this. If you see any lines with colours in them then switch to 48K to edit them and back to 128K to use the disk.

When you break into some OUTLET programs, the listing may not be visible. Practice entering...

POKE 23607,60 ...blindly until it is second nature. This will reveal the listing. An alternate way is to reset and MERGE the program. However, some programs may not permit this.

In almost every case you can save a program to +3 disk using RUN 9972 (BUT YOU MUST BE IN 128 MODE!)

Load the tape issue until the title picture appears.Change the LOAD "" at the end of line 50 to LOAD "CONTENTS". Save on disk.

Load the CONTENTS from tape.

Jot down line 9902 for reference (you might use LLIST 9902 then break in after that line has printed).

Extract lines 20 to 30.

Load a recent CONTENTS. Merge in those lines 20 and 30 and adjust line 9902 ACCORDING TO YOUR BEST JUDGEMENT! Sorry but there may be numerous variations. Save it.

You need a tape header reader to find the size of code files. Try CASSCAT from OUTLET 37. I assume you know how to load and save to disk but you need to change the names of some thus... .

Early text files use the keyword "CODE" as the 10th character and this needs changing to "#". If you find the address and length of the code using CASSCAT as say A and L then try something like:

10 LOAD "T:"

20 SAVE "A:"

10 LOAD "NAME     CODE" CODE A,L

20 SAVE "NAME     #" CODE A,L

The CODE and the # must ALWAYS be the 10th character so put in spaces if needed. You will have to enter the CODE keyword in 48K using EXTEND then I.

Individual programs will probab- ly load and run except where the program loads extra code. This may be OK if the code is named but not if it is simply.... LOAD "" CODE etc. In that case you will need to search for the actual filename using your best judgement!

If you want the individual prog- rams to link back to CONTENTS, NEXT and BOOT properly then study, in 48K, lines 8920 to 8930 in recent programs to see how they work. You might then extract such lines and MERGE them in old programs. HOWEVER, there are many, many variations so lots of possibilities for errors!

On Side B of any recent +3 disk is a file called "DISK". This needs copying to Side B of the disk you are trying to create.It simply loads the CONTENTS on the B side.

This CONTENTS file on Side B is a slightly modified form of the one on Side A.I suggest that you take the one from the same issue you get the Side A from and alt- er it in the same way except line 9902.

In both CONTENTS there are lines at around 91 to 108 that do var- ious things like loading OUTDEX, PROCROSS and the line at 99 which prompts you when to switch to Side B.

You need to alter the value in line 99: PEEK NIF > VAL "14" to the last file you have on Side A.Just for your reference,Item N on the CONTENTS display is 14.

Oh yes! -  Nearly forgot!  Alter the value of H at the start of line 9930 in CONTENTS to the total number of filenames listed in the DATA at line 30. I now have a horrible feeling the DATA may have a different sequence! Compare the originals - you may need to use a recent line 30 and retype the filenames!

Those are only the basic things to worry about but you may get it to work even if not perfectly so good luck!             Brian
